This is one of the two citations the sheet's own wiki page already lists (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, cite_note-eia-2, backlinks:8) -- I opened the live workbook behind that generic landing page. Independently, the harvested Pipeline News / Pipeline & Gas Journal PDF (also already cited by the wiki, cite_note-source1-1) carries a dated (11/17) planning-stage entry: 'STEEL REEF INFRASTRUCTURE CORP. -- Project: South Saskatchewan Access Pipeline ... Location: Portal, ND - North Portal, SK ... Start: 4Q 2018 ... Status: Project is undergoing public meetings.' Two independent origins (EIA federal dataset; trade-press planning tracker), neither GEM-derived, both naming the pipeline by its exact name and describing the same ND-SK crossing -- existence is solid, tier=high. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row US-West roster, especially the Williston/Bakken cluster (P0158 Bison, P0281 Williston Basin, P2099 Northern Border, P0367 Valley Expansion, P3158 Traill County, P0306 Doosan Bobcat) that sits in the same basin. No overlap in operator (all six are WBI Energy/MDU or TC Energy/ONEOK systems; P0316 is Steel Reef, an unrelated midstream company) or route (P0316's 2-2.2mi feeder runs Portal ND to North Portal SK specifically for Steel Reef's own SK processing plant, not into any of those larger transmission systems). Not a duplicate/relabel of any roster row. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 'Steel Reef Infrastructure' [100%] matches PGJ's 'STEEL REEF INFRASTRUCTURE CORP.' (name-variant only, no ownership dispute). Operator was blank on the sheet -- filled below as 'Steel Reef Pipelines US LLC' per EIA's 'Pipeline Operator Name' field, distinct from (subsidiary of) the Owner entity, which is a coherent parent/subsidiary split, not a conflict. CLASSIFICATION (Fuel/commodity): correctly gas, not oil/NGL -- both sources are natural-gas-specific (EIA's gas workbook; Pipeline News gas trade press). Overall: real pipeline, correctly classified as gas, correctly attributed, not a duplicate. The two genuine open items are filed as separate concern records below (Length: 2.00mi vs the sourced 2.2mi; PipelineType classification ambiguity given the FERC CP docket).

I could not reach FERC eLibrary's docket text for CP18-24 (JS-rendered app, blocks scripted/curl access; a second reference to the CP18-24 order itself would be the strongest tie-breaker) or the Canada Energy Regulator's site (site search 404'd) within this session's budget. validity.recommendation: Have a human pull the actual FERC CP18-24 certificate order text and confirm whether the Commission treated this facility as jurisdictional transportation/transmission or exempt gathering; if transportation, consider reclassifying PipelineType off 'gathering'.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records PipelineType=gathering. That is plausible on the functional description in both my sources (EIA: 'Deliver gas to Canada for processing' -- i.e. moving unprocessed gas from area wells to a foreign processing plant, the classic gathering pattern -- rather than moving pipeline-quality gas to a distribution system or end market). But the same EIA record lists Authority=FERC, Docket=CP18-24 -- a full FERC 'CP' certificate docket. Under NGA Section 1(b), true gathering facilities are normally EXEMPT from FERC's Section 7 certificate jurisdiction; needing an actual FERC certificate is at minimum suggestive that FERC's own jurisdictional determination for this specific facility differs from a plain 'gathering' exemption (it may instead reflect Section 3 border-crossing/export authorization, which does not by itself reclassify the functional type -- I could not distinguish the two without the order text). I tried to pull the CP18-24 order itself from elibrary.ferc.gov (a JS-only React app; scripted/curl access returns only an empty shell, no docket content) and from the Canada Energy Regulator's site (cer-rec.gc.ca search paths I tried both 404'd) and could not resolve either within this session's search budget (WebSearch was already exhausted batch-wide before I reached this row; DuckDuckGo/Bing/Google all returned bot-challenge or JS-shell pages under curl, and WebFetch on the same URLs returned unrelated or empty content). Filing this as a low-confidence classification flag rather than a confident reclassification -- I have a real, sourced reason to doubt 'gathering' is the whole story, but not a sourced alternative value, hence the blank contested value.
